correctness.rationale: For every field and finite poset, commuting idempotents define a complete orthogonal spectral family. The explicit unit u=sum_s f_s d_s reduces to 1 modulo the nilpotent diagonal-zero ideal, and ud_s=f_su yields simultaneous conjugacy over every extension. For each fixed coloring the centralizer in 1+J is given by vanishing coefficients at differently colored comparable pairs; this gives orbit dimension and exact F_q cardinality q^m. At canonical tuples, linearized idempotence and commutativity yield precisely one tangent parameter per such pair. The orbit dimension matches the tangent dimension, proving smoothness and irreducible component claims. Edgewise expansion q^(different)=q+(1-q)1_(same) proves the random-cluster expression. Standalone verify.py exhausts all idempotents, commuting tuples, and diagonal-color fibers in eight small cases over F2, F3, and F4, and checks the linearized Jacobian rank for every color. No finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Single-idempotent and single-potent enumerations specialize the tuple problem only when the tuple length is one; these do not by themselves determine fiberwise correlations between two or more idempotents. G-grading theorems concern additional homogeneous decompositions and are not the same moduli problem. The new result is restricted to joint tuples and explicitly includes all characteristic-two cases; nevertheless potential consequences of more general idempotent-lifting theorems remain a historical risk. The length-one idempotent count for odd q is prior-covered via involutions, and the new claim is not its isolated specialization but simultaneous tuple geometry and all-length Potts counts.

value.rationale: The canonical moduli scheme of ordered commuting projections in an arbitrary finite-poset incidence algebra acquires a uniform full component classification, component dimensions, and finite-field point counts. The exact comparability-graph Potts polynomial is natural and reconstructs the Tutte polynomial when parameters range through all fields and tuple lengths. This provides structure across every finite poset and arbitrary characteristic, not a small arbitrary census. The short proof and finite-poset restriction are documented limits, and elementary ingredients alone do not erase the usefulness of the complete joint classification.
